reviewEvidence: Approved against revision-99abdc7f (the repair revision). Three passes. PASS 1 (verify) re-checked every acceptance criterion against the code and reproduced both RED claims by stashing source only. PASS 2 was an INDEPENDENT adversarial review by a fresh-context agent with no memory of the implementation: told to falsify the two strongest claims ("exactly one setup record on every path", "no structured execution path drops stderr any more"), to check each AC against code rather than tests, to sweep for regressions from the two deleted registry fields, and to run the security profile. It verified the security surface clean (no dependency changes in either commit, the installer still runs the fixed SETUP_ARGV behind the unchanged confirm/hasUI gate, the audit writer's redaction covers the new failure paths, and diagnostics reach only the operator UI — never model context, never the audit file) and the regression sweep clean (no remaining configOnly/orphanDockerCandidates/hostCommandIdentity consumer anywhere in code, docs, tests or dist; the new symbols are present in dist). It DID falsify the broader stderr claim and surfaced eight further gaps, every one of which was re-verified against the source before being recorded. PASS 3 is the repair, done under TDD where each slice began with a test whose RED output IS the defect: 'Failed to spawn: devcontainer' without the errno; 'host-out\n' without '--- stderr ---'; 'docker remove failed with exit 1.' without the daemon's own message; 'container out\n' carrying only the stdout half of docker logs; 'npm install exited null' instead of the signal; an undefined errorSummary on both the non-zero-exit and the failed-probe setup records; 'supersecret-token-value' returned unredacted to the operator and the model; 'expected true to be false' for a sub-millisecond timeout that aborted at 0 ms of virtual time; and 'reportDiscoveryDiagnostics is not a function' for the untested drain. All thirteen findings from PASS 2 are fixed and verified: (1) toSpawnError now names the OS error code on every branch and explains ENOTCONN as a PATH-transport fault with a remedy, which is the misdiagnosis this whole phase exists to prevent — four new mapper tests plus a troubleshooting entry; (2) the L2-02 stderr class is closed repo-wide — the /devcontainer host-exec COMMAND, docker logs (whose onStderr count was literally 0, so half of every log read was discarded) and stop/remove failures, which now carry a bounded one-line rendering of what Docker said instead of only the exit code — three new tests; (3) a positive sub-millisecond timeout is floored to 1 ms at both entry points through one resolveTimeoutMs, and sub-second deadlines render in milliseconds rather than as 'timed out after 0s' — fake-timer tests at both layers; (4) a signal-killed install names the signal; (5) the setup record is written once, after the outcome is known, so a failed probe cannot leave a success-shaped record; (6) a failing audit sink is surfaced in the returned result instead of escaping unnormalized; (7) the failure text handed back to the operator and the model is redacted like the audit copy; (8) the discovery drain became a tested policy (reportDiscoveryDiagnostics) and moved into a finally so a throwing verb still reports; (9) the shipped README.zh-CN and the stale tool-output comment are back in sync; (10) three vacuous assertions were deleted and the fourth now states what it pins; (11) the host-path disclosure is documented as operator-only; (12) the drain-skip note is fixed; (13) the documented CLI contract was re-confirmed against the version this host resolves, 0.89.0 — every flag the adapter passes (up/build/exec with --workspace-folder, --docker-path, --config, --container-id, --remote-env) still exists, so the 0.88.0 pin remains conservative rather than wrong. A fourteenth defect was found while fixing those and is fixed too: /devcontainer <verb> produced NO output at all, because Pi's command dispatcher ignores a handler's return value (_tryExecuteExtensionCommand is `return await command.handler(args, ctx), true`) and nothing rendered CommandResult.text, so list/status/logs and friends were silent even though the type documents the text as 'Markdown rendered into the TUI'. Repair verification: npm run typecheck; npm run test:unit (31 files, 344 tests — 23 added); verify-package.mjs --unit-tests (all gates); a rebuilt dist committed and confirmed to match a fresh build; the packed smoke-pi-package.mjs --no-model run; and npm run install:local -- --check. Two seams stay outside unit-test reach and are reported as limitations (below) rather than claimed covered. The previous revision's approval was withdrawn when the repair landed — an approval is bound to a revision id, so editing code after one is approved invalidates it even when the findings themselves were non-blocking — and is restored here against revision-99abdc7f. No blocking or major finding remains open against this revision; the notes below are records and limitations, not defects awaiting repair.

findings.message: Limitation, stated rather than papered over. Two behaviours delivered by this phase live in the extension's command dispatch, which this repository has no unit harness for (the same limitation the Phase 1 review recorded for the engagement path): delivering a handler's rendered result, and draining discovery diagnostics after a verb runs. Their POLICY halves are unit-tested now (`displayCommandResult`, `reportDiscoveryDiagnostics`), and the wiring is exercised by the packed smoke run, which loads the real extension in a real Pi session. Deleting either call site would still leave the suite green, so a future change to the dispatch should be smoke-checked rather than trusting the unit suite.

`kata-cli verify` reports `missingAcceptanceMatrix: true` for this task: the six acceptance criteria exist in `task.json` and each is evaluated, but the machine-readable `acceptanceMatrix` field (implementationPaths / testPaths / evidence / verificationLevel per criterion) was never populated — the real matrix lives in `openspec/changes/arch-review-p2-failure-observability/design.md` §4. This is the same gap the first Kata task recorded in this repository, and it does not block verify or judge, but the judge should decide against the design matrix rather than against the placeholder-free-but-unstructured field.

Deliberate, and now documented. The discovery diagnostics name host paths (an unreadable directory, `maxDepth` pruning, a path resolving outside the allowed root, a container without the Dev Container label). They are operator-UI only — never model context, never the audit file — and are reported once per distinct line per session. `docs/troubleshooting.md` states all of that, so a future change that routes these into model context has to contradict the documentation rather than slip through unnoticed.

Workflow lesson, kept on purpose. When the repair changed task-owned paths after the seal, re-running verify reported all six criteria FAIL with `repairScope: revision_superseded` — the documented "an owned file changed, build the next revision" signal rather than an acceptance failure — and the CLI then refused `build` from the review phase unless the review recorded a blocking finding, so the supersession was written up as exactly that and the task went review -> implement -> a new seal (revision-99abdc7f) -> verify PASS -> this approval. The transferable part: an approval is bound to a revision id and gate choices are single-use, so any post-approval edit costs a full re-seal/re-verify/re-review cycle even when every finding was non-blocking.
